beats.text: The ozone hole was fixed years ago.
beats.note: It is recovering, not recovered. The 2022 UN assessment expects the layer to return to 1980 values by 2040 over most of the world, and around 2066 over Antarctica.

beats.name: Farman, Gardiner and Shanklin
beats.role: British Antarctic Survey scientists whose results showed abnormally low ozone above Halley Bay near the South Pole.

beats.text: Two years later, nations agreed to act.
beats.note: The Montreal Protocol was agreed on 16 September 1987 and entered into force on 1 January 1989.

beats.text: Every UN member state signed up.
beats.note: Wikipedia describes it as the first universally ratified treaty in United Nations history. As of October 2022 that covered every UN member state.

beats.context: Nearly this share of banned ozone depleting substances has been phased out, according to UN News citing the 2022 assessment.

beats.note: UN News says the Protocol has helped avoid an estimated 0.5 degrees Celsius of global warming.

beats.text: A hole found in 1985 may not close until 2066.
